data.A: Refine the fastest measured approach (program 97b103d05aca4f1e, 0.02305 s): preserve the one-row DP and sorted obstacle sweep, and focus on reducing fallback per-cell and obstacle-lookup overhead. Benchmark changes against this candidate across workload sizes; keep the DP correct for every valid obstacle configuration.
data.B: Explore an obstacle-centric algorithm and a defensible crossover to the dense DP fallback. Prior combinatorial candidates measured 0.07372 s and 0.10976 s, while the SIMD hybrid measured 0.05378 s—all slower than the best result—so diagnose their costs rather than carrying them over unchanged. Account for obstacle count, deduplication, endpoint blocks, and modular arithmetic; avoid a quadratic obstacle-pair path when its estimated work exceeds the grid scan.
data.C: Improve the measured anti-diagonal wavefront approach (0.02591 s), which is competitive but slower than the best candidate. On the four-core ARM64 target, investigate tiled wavefront work to reduce per-diagonal synchronization and scheduling overhead, retaining a low-overhead sequential path for small workloads. Preserve the true DP dependencies and validate all obstacle cases.
data.G: Use the fastest measured candidate, A's 97b103d05aca4f1e, as the integration baseline. Incorporate B or C ideas only when their isolated measurements justify them, with a workload-based dispatch if needed; do not assume their gains add when combined. Measure and correctness-check the complete integrated program, including small grids, duplicate obstacles, and blocked endpoints, against the same harness.
data.analysis: This is Problem D: the baseline uses O(N²) blocked-cell storage and O(N²) DP work. The strongest measured candidate replaces dense obstacle storage with a sorted obstacle sweep and one-row DP, reducing mean time from 0.07983 s to 0.02305 s. The wavefront candidate measured 0.02591 s; the in-place DP candidate measured 0.04788 s. Other measured combinatorial/SIMD variants were slower (0.05378–0.10976 s), so further algorithmic branches need evidence and a crossover that reflects their actual costs. Favor measured, correctness-preserving improvements; do not assume integration is additive.
